wasteland-street-winter.notes: Previous failure resolved. The conspicuous dark pools and long crossing slush swipes from critic-r105-2 are gone. The 3x3 field at 1x and 4x has short irregular grey rubble/slush patches, restrained buried cracks and no hard edge seam, visible cell grid or dominant 288px pool/chevron motif. A diagonal grain remains, but its short low-contrast clusters behave like the approved winter terrain texture and stay subordinate to isolated small shacks as well as dense buildings. All four 8x quadrants and the wrap-cross crop retain hard pixel clusters; winter has surface information rather than a blank blue-grey fill. The colder, dirtier snow is appropriate to wasteland and does not clash with the white/blue roof snow.

general_findings: All 78 required assets are present at the prescribed dimensions. All 76 sprites use binary transparency, are centred within 0.5 source pixel, and end on row height-2. Both bases are completely opaque.

At native size the shacks, patched homes, markets, water towers, tanks, conveyor and foundry remain distinguishable. Distinct rooflines, heights, additions and openings survive random one-cell planting and dense grouping. No exact duplicate sprites or visually interchangeable variant pair found; summer/winter counterparts intentionally preserve architecture.

Dark contours and stepped silhouette edges are clean on the checker and actual ground. No visible halo/fringe or blur; no partial-alpha pixels. Local chips and roof dither in some unchanged sprites remain subordinate to identifiable material planes and openings at 1x.

Top and left-facing planes keep the light emphasis. Rust/tan concrete/olive-grey sheet patches fit the approved wasteland markers; warmer scrap buildings also sit within the approved round-2 material palette. Every winter counterpart has visible roof/ledge accumulation, with access gaps and openings still readable.

The only changed file, the winter street base, now meets the calm-ground requirement. Directional snow texture by itself is not a failure: the revised short irregular clusters no longer create the previous dominant recurring pools or crossing chevron bands, and do not compete with small planted structures.
_review.evidence_notes: All scales use nearest-neighbour enlargement. Labels and transparency checker are review apparatus. Contact sheets cover each sprite at 1x/4x; paired sheets cover each sprite at 8x. Full 3x3 base fields and full dense-to-sparse scenes were viewed at 1x/4x; saved 4x bands/panels are also available for close inspection. Approved comparison art receives no pass/fail verdict.
